text:
lina: PSA: learned the hard way  do not delete your email with the mobile boarding pass until you're past security. Phone died at the gate and the airline app logged me out. Panic ensued. 62d
harry: Oof. Did you have it in Apple Wallet / Google Wallet? Those usually survive logouts.
tia: I screenshot mine and keep the PDF copy in a locked notes app. Screenshots work 90% of the time but some airlines want the live pass barcode.
ben: Gate agents are usually chill if you can show the booking reference + photo ID. But at small regional gates they can be strict. Learned that at a puddle jumper once.
ops-bot: Reminder: travel checklist -> add "email boarding pass saved" and "screenshot backup" items. https://drive.example/travel-checklist
lina: The worst was airport battery anxiety while trying to re-open the app. Ended up asking to borrow a charger from the info desk (life-saver).
harry: Pro tip: keep a 10k powerbank at gate. Also carry a 2-minute wired charger in your pocket. Wireless can be too slow at low battery.
tia: Also, if you're on Android, `pass2` apps sometimes re-add passes from emails automatically. On iPhone, double-check Wallet permissions.
ben: For the offsite, can we add a tiny "phone survival kit" to the team bag: 1 powerbank, 2 short cables (USB-C/Lightning), and a few adhesive cable ties? Vote :thumbsup: / :thumbsdown:
harry: :thumbsup: from me. Add a reusable phone charger pouch too.
lina: Agreed. And maybe a printed sheet with booking ref + last 4 of CC for emergencies (keep it in the team lead's travel folder).
tia: For memes: saw a guy at SFO queueing in a huddle, phone in a Ziploc like it was a lifeboat. Photo submitted to #random-memes.
ben: Kudos to the gate agent who helped me after my phone died — they reprinted my boarding pass and handed me a granola bar. Human kindness = travel fuel. :heart:
ops-bot: Noted: "phone survival kit" added to shared travel items.
